Donald Trump has reportedly issued Nato allies with an ultimatum to send warships to the Strait of Hormuz within days, as his ceasefire with Iran comes under risk of collapse.

Nato boss Mark Rutte told European leaders that Trump expects partners to make concrete military commitments, according to Der Spiegel, casting the demand as an ‘ultimatum’.

It came amid reports that Trump was drawing up a list of partners that supported or opposed his war in the Middle East, weighing the removal of US forces from countries deemed resistant.

In another outburst on social media earlier in the day, the president lamented that “NATO WASN’T THERE WHEN WE NEEDED THEM, AND THEY WON’T BE THERE IF WE NEED THEM AGAIN. REMEMBER GREENLAND, THAT BIG, POORLY RUN, PIECE OF ICE!!!” [sic]

open image in gallery Donald Trump’s ceasefire hangs by a thread as Benjamin Netanyahu faces backlash for Israel’s actions in Lebanon ( Getty )

Trump’s fragile ceasefire in the Middle East looked on the verge of collapse, meanwhile, with Iran threatening to pull out of talks if Israel presses on with attacks against Hezbollah in Lebanon. Iran accuses the US and Israel of flouting the ceasefire agreement, which they deny.

Israel maintains its military operation is aimed at defeating Hezbollah but experts have warned the action could lead to a similar humanitarian crisis to Gaza.

“Whoever acts against Israeli civilians will be struck,” Netanyahu said in a defiant statement on Thursday as condemnations poured in. “We will continue to strike Hezbollah wherever required, until we restore full security to the residents of the north.”

However, hours later Netanyahu appearing to shift his tone dramatically and said he had instructed his cabinet to start direct negotiations with Lebanon as soon as possible.

More than 1,700 people have been killed in Lebanon over the past six weeks, including over 250 in major strikes on Wednesday. Over one million people, 20 per cent of Lebanon’s population, has already been displaced in six weeks.

Iran’s deputy prime minister, Dr Saeed Khatibzadeh, called Israel’s action a “grave violation” of the agreement and said “the coming hours are very critical” as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps hints they will restart fighting if the attacks on Lebanon do not stop.

open image in gallery The site of an Israeli strike carried out on Wednesday, in Al-Mazraa in Beirut, Lebanon ( Reuters )

Dr Khatibzadeh said on Thursday that Iran was on the verge of responding to what it considered to be ceasefire violations on Wednesday night but Pakistan intervened to prevent an escalation.

The IRGC said it would enact a “regret-inducing” response to the attacks if they continued with state media quoting an official saying: “Any attack on the proud Hezbollah is an attack on Iran.”

Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian added: “Iran will not abandon the Lebanese people”. Sensitivities were further heightened as Iranians turned up in droves to mourn 40 days since supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed in US-Israeli attacks on 28 February.

President Donald Trump said that American military personnel would remain stationed around the region until the agreement is “fully complied with and that “bigger, and better, and stronger” attacks would follow if it was breached.

Oil prices surged again in response to the confusion after initially plummeting following the ceasefire announcement earlier this week.

open image in gallery A worker paints a road separator near the Serena Hotel, the expected venue for US-Iran talks, in the Red Zone area of Islamabad on April 9, 2026. ( AFP/Getty )

Multiple ship tracking sources including Lloyd’s List Intelligence and Kpler said that movement through the Strait of Hormuz remains at a standstill.

Iran warned that ships transiting through the vital waterway may be hit by “anti-ship mines in the main transit routes” due to the “state of war” as it advised vessels to follow alternative paths.

The Navy stressed all vessels must stay in touch with security forces to avoid “potential collisions with naval mines.”

Peace talks are due to take place at the Serena Hotel in Pakistan’s capital Islamabad on Saturday with vice president JD Vance due to lead a US delegation according to Axios, and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s parliamentary speaker to lead the Iranians, according to reports.

But Tehran has also threatened to walk away from the process entirely, citing Israeli violations of the ceasefire as grounds to withdraw, sources told the Wall Street Journal.

open image in gallery Trump has reportedly demanded European allies act to secure the Strait of Hormuz ( AFP via Getty )

Israel’s actions have sparked international outrage with Britain’s foreign secretary Yvette Cooper condemning the escalation as “deeply damaging” and calling for Lebanon to be “urgently included” in the agreement.

The European Union’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas criticised the number of civilian deaths in Lebanon and said it was becoming “hard to argue that such heavy-handed actions fall within self-defence”. Kallas called on the ceasefire agreement to be extended to Lebanon.

President Emmanuel Macron and French foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the agreement must cover Lebanon as France condemned “massive” Israeli strikes.

Barrot said Iran must give up the right to have nuclear weapons, surrender its use of missiles and drones to threaten other countries in the region and stop supporting groups including Hezbollah, Hamas and the Houthis.

Germany’s chancellor Friedrich Merz said his country had taken up direct talks again with the Iranian leadership in Tehran and said he does not want “Nato to break apart” amid the crisis and said he had encouraged President Trump to pursue negotiations “with urgency”.

Netanyahu is also facing backlash within Israel with opposition leaders calling his actions in Iran and Lebanon a historical “disaster”.

The defence secretary has issued a stark warning to Vladimir Putin after Russian attack and spy submarines were found operating in the North Atlantic.

John Healey told a press conference in Downing Street on Thursday that in the past few weeks, while many eyes were trained on the Middle East crisis, the UK responded to “increased Russian activity” near crucial UK cables and pipelines in the Atlantic north of Britain.

He revealed that the UK and allies monitored the vessels – which included a Russian Akula-class nuclear-powered attack submarine and two specialist submarines from Russia’s ministry of defence deep sea research programme, known as GUGI – for a month before they retreated.

Addressing Putin directly, Mr Healey said: “We see your activity over our cables and our pipelines, and you should know that any attempt to damage them will not be tolerated and will have serious consequences.”

open image in gallery Defence secretary John Healey says the Russian submarines were tracked for a month ( Toby Shepheard/PA )

Mr Healey’s warning comes after The Telegraph reported that Russia sent a warship to escort sanctioned oil tankers through the English Channel, following Sir Keir Starmer’s declaration that sanctioned vessels sailing in British waters would be seized.

Black Sea Fleet frigate Admiral Grigorovich is said to have accompanied a pair of shadow fleet ships on Wednesday, which were followed by a British naval vessel.

open image in gallery Satellite imagery of the Russian GUGI vessels at dock ( Ministry of Defence )

According to the newspaper, the vessel observed the flotilla off England’s south coast while RFA Tideforce, a Royal Fleet Auxiliary tanker, was in their wake.

Mr Healey said: “In response to the Russian submarines, I can confirm that I deployed our armed forces to track and to deter any malign activity by these vessels.

“A Royal Navy warship and Royal Air Force P8 aircraft alongside allies ensured that the Russian submarines were monitored 24/7.

“The Akula submarine subsequently retreated home, having been closely tracked throughout and we continued to monitor the two GUGI submarines in and around wider UK waters.

“Our armed forces left them in no doubt that they were being monitored, that their movements were not covert, as President Putin planned, and that their attempted secret operation had been exposed.

“Those GUGI submarines have now left UK waters and headed back north.”

The defence secretary said the attack submarine acted as “a likely decoy” to distract us from the GUGI submarines as they “spent time over critical infrastructure relevant to us and our allies in the North Atlantic”.

He continued: “Because we were watching them, we wanted to ensure that we could warn them that their covert operation had been exposed and reduce the risk that they may attempt any action that could damage our pipelines or our cables.

“And I’m confident, we have no evidence that there has been any damage, but with allies, we’re sure that this is now verifiable.”

Undersea fibre-optic cables, which are responsible for 99 per cent of the world’s digital communications, are essential for commerce, government and military functions because they securely transport messages and information. Any damage to Britain’s undersea cables could cause serious political and economic disruption.

The Russian action comes after the prime minister last month said that the navy would intercept its shadow fleet. The armed forces and British law enforcement are now able to halt and board sanctioned vessels that are passing through UK waters.

Sir Keir’s announcement was made in conjunction with European allies in an attempt to cut off funding for Moscow’s war with Ukraine.

It is understood that Russia’s shadow fleet consists of approximately 700 vessels, carrying around 40 per cent of all Russian oil exports. The UK has sanctioned 544 Russian shadow fleet vessels to date.

They illegally ship oil and other goods out of Russia by flying the flags of other countries, with the aim of evading sanctions imposed by the West since the invasion of Ukraine began.

Sir Keir gave approval for British forces to begin seizing Russian shadow fleet tankers on 26 March.

open image in gallery Prime minister Keir Starmer earlier this year warned that sanctioned vessels sailing in British waters would be seized ( PA Wire )

Closing off British waters is aimed at forcing the Russian vessels into taking longer, more costly sea routes, or risk being intercepted by the UK.

Sir Keir said: “We are living in an increasingly volatile and dangerous world, facing threats from different fronts across the world every day.

“As prime minister, my first duty is to keep this country safe and protect British interests here and abroad.

“Putin is rubbing his hands at the war in the Middle East because he thinks higher oil prices will let him line his pockets.

“That’s why we’re going after his shadow fleet even harder, not just keeping Britain safe but starving Putin’s war machine of the dirty profits that fund his barbaric campaign in Ukraine.

“He and his cronies should be in no doubt, we will always defend our sovereignty and stand with Ukraine for as long as it takes.”

British forces have already been involved in tracking shadow fleet vessels for several years, and have supported operations by other countries to seize the ships.

Benjamin Netanyahu is facing a domestic backlash over the Pakistan-brokered two-week ceasefire deal with Iran, with critics accusing him of presiding over “the worst political disaster in history”.

The Israeli prime minister is facing an onslaught from parties across the country’s political spectrum for not continuing the conflict, although Tel Aviv was not involved in the peace talks.

There is also a growing international outcry over ongoing Israeli strikes on Lebanon, which, as of Thursday, have killed 1,700 people including 130 children. Western countries have insisted that Lebanon must be part of the ceasefire, while Tehran has claimed that attacks on the country represent a “grave violation” of the agreement.

open image in gallery Netanyahu is increasingly isolated on the world and domestic stage ( AFP/Getty )

The developments have sparked outrage among Israeli politicians, who have urged Mr Netanyahu to continue the war. Opposition leader Yair Lapid branded the Israeli PM’s handling of the conflict a catastrophe.

“There has never been such a political disaster in all of our history,” he wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. “Israel wasn’t even at the table when decisions were made concerning the core of our national security.”

He praised the military for carrying out “everything that was asked of it” and the public for demonstrating “amazing resilience”, but said they had both been let down by Mr Netanyahu due to what he called the leader’s “arrogance, negligence and lack of strategic planning”.

Mr Lapid’s criticism was repeated by former prime minister Naftali Bennett, who said Israel’s failure to achieve its war goals would leave it “facing a vengeful Iran”.

“The reason why so many people feel disappointed tonight is that the leadership sold us illusions,” he said in a live broadcast on Wednesday.

“All their empty promises have exploded in our faces. Unfortunately, each of us sees with our own eyes that Hamas is getting stronger. Hezbollah and Iran are standing on their own two feet, and this is happening because a government that dismantles Israel from within cannot defeat the enemy from without.”

Yair Golan, centre-left politician and the head of the Democrats party, accused Mr Netanyahu of lying.

“He promised a ‘historic victory’ and security for generations, and in practice, we got one of the gravest strategic failures Israel has known,” he said in a post on X, adding: “Blood was spilled ... brave citizens killed (and) soldiers fell ... none of the goals were accomplished.”

open image in gallery Lapid has called Netanyahu’s strategy a ‘political disaster’ ( AP )

“The nuclear program was not destroyed; the ballistic threat remains; the regime is in place and is even stronger coming out of this war,” he continued.

Mr Netanyahu’s education minister Yoav Kisch hit back at the critics, accusing them of “pumping up a defeat that’s echoed in the enemy’s media outlets”.

The Israeli PM has also faced a growing international outcry over the IDF’s campaign in Lebanon, which aid agencies warn has created a humanitarian catastrophe. More than 250 people have been killed in 24 hours in the deadliest attacks on the country since the conflict began.

More than 100 sites were targeted in 10 minutes on Wednesday and more than a million people (20 per cent of the population) has been displaced since the attacks began in late February.

Despite a ceasefire being agreed on Wednesday, Mr Netanyahu and the White House said that the 14-day truce does not apply to Lebanese territory – a key demand for Tehran.

open image in gallery Netanyahu and Trump both acted jointly in declaring war on Iran ( Getty )

Israel says it must continue its attacks in order to defeat Hezbollah, an Iran-backed proxy group. However, large numbers of civilians have been killed and humanitarian groups have warned there are similarities to the IDF’s campaign in Gaza.

Spain, France and the UK have all called for the ceasefire to be extended to Lebanon.

Britain’s foreign minister Yvette Cooper called for the country to be “urgently included” and on Thursday called Israel’s attacks “highly damaging”, following similar comments by French president Emmanuel Macron.

The European Union’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas criticised the number of civilian deaths in Lebanon and said it was becoming “hard to argue that such heavy-handed actions fall within self-defence”.

open image in gallery More than 200 people were killed in one day in Lebanon on Wednesday after Israel’s deadliest strikes yet ( Reuters )

Mr Trump has also come under fire in Israel for agreeing a ceasefire.

“Donald, you came off as a duck,” said the far-right head of the country’s National Security Committee, Tzvika Foghel in a since-deleted post on X.

The head of the conservative Yisrael Beytenu party, Avigdor Liberman, said the agreement with Iran “gives the ayatollah’s regime a break and time to regroup”.

“Any agreement with Iran, without giving up on destroying Israel, enriching uranium, manufacturing ballistic missiles and supporting terror groups in the region, means we’ll return to another war in harder conditions with a heavier price,” he wrote on X.

News.content:

The U.S. Postal Service said Thursday it has informed federal budget officials it will temporarily suspend its employer contributions to Federal Employees Retirement System annuities, allowing it to keep making payroll, paying suppliers and delivering the mail.

The step taken by the Postal Board of Governors is meant to preserve cash and liquidity due to the Postal Service's ”ongoing, severe financial crisis," Postal Service Chief Financial Officer Luke Grossmann said in an internal message to USPS employees. Officials have warned the USPS is on course to run out of cash by around February 2027.

Despite the suspension of employer contributions, effective Friday, current and future retirees will not be immediately impacted, Grossman said.

“The risk to the Postal Service and the American public from insufficient liquidity for postal operations dramatically outweighs any longer-term risk to the pension funds from not making the currently due payments,” he said in the statement. USPS deferred payments in 2011 during another financial crisis.

The Postal Service said it will continue transmitting employees’ retirement contributions to the federal Office of Personnel Management, along with Thrift Savings Plan contributions, including employer automatic and matching funds, and will also maintain its employer contributions to Social Security.

Brian Renfroe, president of the National Association of Letter Carriers, said the temporary suspension of annuity payments is “not ideal" but it doesn't immediately impact his members, who he said understand the Postal Service's financial challenges.

“Given a menu of options, none of which are overall positive, they would certainly prefer the Postal Service making a move like this as opposed to something that immediately impacts them or immediately impacts in a negative way the service that we provide to the American people.”

Ninety-nine percent of career USPS employees are covered by the Federal Employees Retirement System.

Last month, Postmaster General David Steiner told The Associated Press and later a congressional committee that the 250-year-old service needs to have a decades-old cap on borrowing lifted so the independent agency can have access to more cash.

“That will buy us the time to make the fixes we need to make, and we can sail on down the road,” he told the AP. Steiner has called for other changes as well, including giving the Postal Service authority to raise postage prices high enough to cover losses.

Keep Us Posted, an advocacy group representing consumers, catalogs, greeting card publishers and others, has urged Congress to ensure any rate increases would be limited to once a year. The group also wants to ensure six-day-a-week mail service remains and that USPS regulators have greater control over any service changes.

The Postal Service has seen annual volume plummet from about 220 billion pieces in 2006 to about 110 billion today as more people pay bills and communicate online.

USPS’s net losses for the 2025 fiscal year totaled $9 billion, even though total operating revenue increased by $916 million or 1.2%, due largely to its Ground Advantage shipping service. Net losses in fiscal year 2024 were $9.5 billion.

News.title: World economy faces growth shock, IMF warns
News.content:
The International Monetary Fund is poised to slash global growth forecasts as the Iran war wreaks long-lasting harm on the world economy.

Kristalina Georgieva, the fund’s managing director, said growth had been picking up pace before the war but that the conflict had utterly derailed any economic optimism.

“Had it not been for this shock, we would have been upgrading global growth. But now, even our most hopeful scenario involves a growth downgrade. Why? Because of infrastructure damage, supply disruptions, losses of confidence and other scarring effects,” she said.

“Even in a best case, there will be no neat and clean return to the status quo ante.”

It could take five years to restore Qatar’s Ras Laffan gas complex to full capacity after an Iranian missile strike, she noted, while vessels may avoid the Strait of Hormuz for years to come.

Ms Georgieva cited the fact that ship crossings through the Red Sea’s Bab-el-Mandeb strait remain at around half their level before Houthi attacks on vessels in 2023, adding: “We don’t truly know what the future holds for transits through the Strait of Hormuz or, for that matter, for the recovery of regional air traffic.”

Iran’s closure of the strait, which the world relies on for a fifth of its oil and gas supplies, has unleashed a global energy crisis. Oil prices are rising again as a ceasefire appears to be fracturing just a day after being announced.

Ms Georgieva said that “countries directly disrupted by the war – including oil and gas exporters who suffered the blockade – and countries relying on imported oil and gas still bear the brunt of the impact”.

Britain is a net importer of oil and gas, which suggests it will be among those suffering painful downgrades to already underwhelming growth forecasts when the IMF releases its latest forecasts next week.

News.title: Five essential things to know before you board a Disney Cruise Line ship
News.content:
Disney brought its enchanting brand of magic to the high seas by way of Disney Cruise Line in 1998, with Captain Mickey Mouse at the helm. The fleet has since grown to eight ships, which resemble floating versions of the entertainment giant’s famous theme parks, packed with fun and full-on entertainment programmes.

Elegant décor and classical styling brings an upmarket feel that gives a nod to the golden age of sea travel, and extends Disney’s appeal to grown-ups who can enjoy the surprisingly extensive child-free areas on each ship. Onboard attractions – water-coaster rides, nightly Disney-themed musicals, artwork that bursts into life and a real-time talking turtle – exemplify the innovative twists this legendary brand is renowned for.

These frills translate into cruises which are generally higher priced than other family-friendly lines, but such is the cost of tapping into a world where onboard experiences are sprinkled with fairy dust.

News.title: From lockdown to Los Angeles: the rise and rise of South Sudan’s blind footballers
News.content:
Like many great and unusual ideas the inspiration for founding South Sudan’s first blind football team came during lockdown.

It was 2020 and Simon Madol Akol was looking for ways to help the disability inclusion charity Light for the World when he discovered the sport. Able to see himself, he had no idea that it could be played by people without vision. But the opportunity was there.

“This is possible,” he remembers thinking. “This is something that can be done.”

The team’s beginnings were humble, but it was always ambitious. Named the Bright Stars – just like South Sudan’s national team – at the start it had just two players.

One of them was current captain Martin Lado, who was born with limited vision but remembers promising himself to pour energy and focus into the team, hoping that “one day it will make us proud”.

From these origins, the team has gone on to win an international championship in Uganda and is now training for the Paralympics.

But all this was yet to come, and first, they had to learn the rules of the game.

News.title: Liverpool refuse to wave white flag, but don’t bet on another famous comeback
News.content:
Van Dijk, who has won eight major trophies during his eight years with Liverpool, said that the team had let down both their manager and the fans, before pointedly adding: “But also you shouldn’t give up, and that’s maybe what happened at a certain point.”

Upon arriving at the Parc des Princes for their Champions League quarter-final first leg against defending Paris St Germian, Wirtz was also asked if the players still had faith in Slot, whose position has come under enormous scrutiny following Saturday’s defeat. With the gap to Arsenal in the Premier League now 21 points, the Champions League is Liverpool’s last remaining hope of a trophy this season.

Asked if they were still playing for the manager, Wirtz said: “Yes of course we are believing in the manager. The team should believe in the manager because they won the league last season. We have a lot of good games this season.”

Slot himself was more nuanced in responding to Van Dijk’s comments, claiming that Liverpool had actually played well in going toe-to-toe with Manchester City for the opening 35 minutes. “Usually in football moments that hurt you most are just before half time and just after half time,” said Slot of City’s burst of goals between the 39th and 57th minute.

“[At 3-0] I saw indeed five minutes in between where it was too open and players were struggling. After the 4-0, City seemed to be OK with the 4-0. We had the ball. Not able to create that much any more. I didn’t see players giving up in the part of the game

“But I think it’s also good from a captain that he has a strong and firm reaction after a game like that. Hopefully it’s not only immediately after a game and we can as a team show a strong and firm reaction.

“[It was] the only four chances we gave away in the game by the way. The good thing is that during this year we have become quite experienced in terms of negativity because of all the setbacks we have had this season.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Bryan Robson laughs as he trolls Liverpool live on ITV’s coverage of Grand National Festival at Aintree
Sports.content:
BRYAN ROBSON joked “I’m so sorry for them” when asked about Liverpool’s 2-0 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain last night.

The former Manchester United captain, 69, headed to Merseyside to enjoy a day of racing at Aintree.





During his trip to the races, Robson chatted with SunSport’s Matt Chapman live on ITV’s coverage of the event.

Cheekily asked if he’d been celebrating Liverpool’s defeat, Robson laughed as he said: “No… I’m so sorry for them.”

When Chapman joked that they’d have a “police escort” ready for the ex-United hero, Robson went on: “Liverpool were up against a really good team.

“PSG are one of the best, play some fantastic football. The movement and passing and everything is really good.

“I like to see the English teams do really well in the Champions League because it makes success for everybody.

“They struggled last night… but I do like to see English teams do well.”

Liverpool fell behind on 11 minutes via Desire Doue’s deflected shot, before Khvicha Kvaratskhelia doubled PSG’s advantage in the second half.

Things could have gotten even worse for Arne Slot‘s men, had PSG been awarded one of two big penalty shouts.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Robson earned 90 England caps during his distinguished international career and Chapman was eager to hear his thoughts on the Three Lions’ chances at this summer’s World Cup – while pointing to Italy‘s failure to qualify as a potential omen.

The ex-England hero added: “When you’ve got an Italian team that three times have not qualified for the World Cup, you’ve got to look and say anything can happen in this game.

“England have got an outside chance.

“I would like to see us be a bit better defensively but other than that I think we’ve got a great midfield and great forwards.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legend, 37, lands shock new job for World Cup 2026 after four months unemployed
Sports.content:
FORMER Manchester United star striker has walked into a surprising new job following FOUR months of unemployment.

Fox Sports announced on Thursday that Mexico’s all-time top goalscorer, Javier “Chicharito” Hernandez, will join their broadcast team for the World Cup 2026.





The centre-forward, 37, will join the likes of Thierry Henry and Zlatan Ibrahimovic while speaking in his second language on the show.

To The Athletic, Hernandez said: “Before I was doing things with my feet.

“Now it’s going to be with my voice.”

“I’m a rookie, man. I cannot promise anything.

“It’s going to be my first time. I don’t know how it’s going to be. I can be very, very positive. I can be very critical, as well.”

The forward – with 109 caps – netted 52 times for Mexico.

But he began his professional career in Guadalajara before he moved to Man Utd.

From 2010 to 2015, Hernandez spent his time at Old Trafford racking up more than 100 appearances at the club.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He then went to Real Madrid on loan for the 2014/15 season, before heading to the Bundesliga to play for Bayer Leverkusen.

But only TWO years after leaving the EFL, the forward was back in the Premier League playing for West Ham.

And after a decade in Europe and a stint with LA Galaxy, Hernandez returned home to Chivas in January 2024 – but the fairytale quickly fell flat.

The former Mexico striker struggled with injuries and poor form, scoring just four goals in 41 games before his deal expired in December.

Chivas confirmed his exit soon after and he hasn’t played a competitive match since.



But Hernandez has insisted he’s not done yet, shutting down talk of retirement.

But now he’ll make his first steps in the world of TV.

Hernandez was hopeful about Mexico’s World Cup chances as they prepare to kick off the tournament against South Africa in a repeat of the 2010 opener.

The ex-striker, who came off the bench in that clash, praised the squad’s passion and discipline under boss Javier Aguirre.

He admitted fans can be fickle but hopes the home support will get behind the team.



Hernandez said: “I’m hoping Mexico can win their group.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And from there, you never know.”

Mexico face South Africa, South Korea and the Czech Republic in Group A with all matches set to be played on home soil.

Sports.title: EFL club’s new stadium hit by High Court legal challenge in major blow to £130million plans
Sports.content:
OXFORD UNITED’S stadium dreams are hanging in the balance after a dramatic legal challenge was lodged in the High Court.

A high-stakes battle has been launched to block the U’s proposed new home, with campaigners sensationally claiming the council acted unlawfully.





Community group Friends of Stratfield Brake (FoSB) have filed court proceedings against Cherwell District Council over the controversial move to build on green belt land.

The ambitious project would see Oxford move to a 16,000-seat stadium on a site known as “the Triangle” between Kidlington and Oxford.

Plans for the site also include a hotel, restaurant, and conference centre right next to woodland at Stratfield Brake.

But local residents have pushed back hard, raising the alarm over potential environmental damage and match-day traffic chaos.



FoSB say they repeatedly warned the council during the planning process.

Their lawyers, Leigh Day, even sent a formal legal letter outlining objections.

They claim those concerns were ignored and have now asked the courts to quash the planning permission.

A massive sticking point involves Natural England, who claimed it was unclear if the nearby woodland is ancient.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Locals also argue the council relied on unproven “assumptions” regarding road closures and how quickly traffic measures could be cleared.

FoSB insists these issues were crucial to the decision and says the approval should never have been granted.

Ricardo Gama, human rights partner at law firm Leigh Day, said: “Our clients felt they had no choice but to file court proceedings.

“They look forward to putting their arguments to a judge.”

On the pitch, Oxford sit just above crisis-hit Sheffield Wednesday in the Championship table, as they battle to avoid the drop.



With five games left, they may need a couple of wins before turning their attention to the courtroom.

The case now moves to the next stage, where a judge will decide whether it proceeds to a full hearing.

Any interested party in English planning decisions can challenge a decision in the High Court.

If the FoSB are successful then a hearing would be held at the Royal Courts of Justice with arguments presented by both sides.

Sports.title: Arsenal files: Gunners outcast in talks over permanent exit and Max Dowman claims another record
Sports.content:
HAMBURG are planning to hold talks with Arsenal over a permanent move for Fabio Vieira.

The midfielder joined the German club on loan last summer and he has been in fine form this season.



Vieira, 25, has scored five goals and provided the same number of assists in 23 Bundesliga appearances.



That has helped Hamburg climb to 12th in the table and they should avoid relegation after being promoted last year.

The German side would love to keep hold of Vieira and the loan agreement they struck with Arsenal has a buy option in it.

Hamburg can make the midfielder’s move permanent for €20million (£17.4m) at the end of this season.

They may be reluctant to pay that full amount, though, and talks with Arsenal are due to take place.

The Gunners signed Vieira from Porto in the summer of 2022 as part of a deal worth an initial £30m.

He will have one year left on his contract at the end of this season and Arsenal are ready to cash in on him.

Vieira’s good form means the Gunners could stand firm on Hamburg paying the full amount of his buy option as other clubs will likely be interested.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Prior to joining Hamburg last summer, Vieira was a target for fellow German side Stuttgart.



LISBON LIE-IN

ARSENAL remained in Lisbon after their 1-0 Champions League win on Tuesday and they did a recovery session early Wednesday before returning home.

Players always prefer returning home straight after the game as they often struggle to sleep.

However, Portugal is known for having some strict rules for flying late in the evening and airports are not always open.

Arsenal played in Braga in November 2010 – they lost 2-0 – and nearby Porto airport was not open after the match.

Arsene Wenger’s squad, along with the media who used to travel with the club in those days, had to take buses to Vigo airport in Spain to return back to Luton after the game.



CAN’T WAIT TO SEE BLUE

SPORTING star Geovany Quenda is joining Chelsea this summer – and could become a fan favourite before he has kicked a ball for the Blues.

The winger, 18, missed the first leg of Sporting’s Champions League quarter-final with Arsenal on Tuesday – which they lost 1-0.

Quenda has been out of action since December after he fractured one of the metatarsal bones in his right foot.

The teenager is back in training now, though, and hopes to play a part when Sporting head to the Emirates on Wednesday.



Quenda is joining Chelsea this summer for £40m and Blues fans would love to see him dump Arsenal out of the Champions League.

The winger actually spent part of his rehab at Chelsea’s training ground in Cobham, where he was able to use their state-of-the-art facilities.

It also allowed the teenager to spend time with his close friend, Blues midfielder Dario Essugo, who is another product of Sporting’s famous youth academy.

TAKE IT TO THE MAX

ANOTHER week, another few firsts and records for Max Dowman to tick off.



The teenager became the youngest player to appear in the knockout stages of the Champions League on Tuesday.

Dowman came on in the 76th minute during Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Sporting at the age of 16 years and 97 days – and has now taken Lamine Yamal’s record.

That was not all for the Gunners youngster this week, though, as he also scooped his first ever Arsenal Goal of the Month award.

Dowman claimed 42 per cent of the vote in the battle for Arsenal’s best goal during the month of March thanks to his stunning solo run against Everton.



The Full Arsenal on YouTube SunSport have launched a dedicated Arsenal channel on YouTube! The Full Arsenal Podcast is your home for everything about the Gunners. From match reactions and tactical breakdowns to transfer talk, match previews, tactical analysis and honest fan debate… The Full Arsenal covers it all. Subscribe to The Full Arsenal here

‘ELL OF A JOB

JAMES ELLIS has left his role as Arsenal technical director after a few months although it looks as though he will not be out of work for long.

Bristol City and Norwich are among the clubs who he has spoken to and it seems there might be a few others who will also show an interest.

Ellis could potentially be heading to Ashton Gate as sporting director in the summer and that man will be handed the job of appointing a full-time boss with Roy Hodgson currently the caretaker.

Norwich are looking for a technical director with former player and manager Neil Adams leaving the club at the end of this season.

The Canaries sporting director is Ben Knapper and he knows Ellis well from his spell as loans manager at Arsenal – and they have remained in constant contact over the last couple of years.



LONDON CALLING?

MAXI ARAUJO caused a few problems for Arsenal flying down the left for Sporting Lisbon – and he could be coming to England this summer.

Incredibly, 12 Premier League scouts watched him impress for Uruguay in their 1-0 win against the Three Lions at Wembley a couple of weeks ago.

Although officially a left-back, he often plays as a winger and he certainly gave Ben White a test in Lisbon.

With Riccardo Calafiori, the versatile Piero Hincapie and Myles Lewis-Skelly all able to play in that position, Arsenal look well-stocked at left-back.

However, if Mikel Arteta allows Lewis-Skelly to leave on loan and sees Hincapie more of a central defender, there could be an opening.



FINE CHINA

ARSENAL Under-15s have booked their place in the final of the Next Gen Beijing Cup after a flawless display.

The travelling Young Guns have won all three of their group stages matches as they toppled Shijiazhuang Kung Fu, Aston Villa and a Beijing FA selected team.

And the academy stars have done it without conceding a single goal.

They will now participate in Saturday’s final, where they will take on Zhejiang Professionals for a chance to lift the trophy.



The tournament has seen highly-rated teenager Luis Munoz continue to impress.

Munoz, 14, scored after just 30 SECONDS in Arsenal’s 3-0 victory over Aston Villa.

The rising star is still technically an Under-14s player, but is playing above his age group on the tour.

Munoz has already represented the U18s and U19s this season, and was recently called up to train with the first-team.



SKY HIGH

FLIGHT prices from London to Spain have SKYROCKETED after Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Sporting in the Champions League quarter-final first leg.

The Gunners are firm favourites to advance after securing a one-goal advantage in Portugal ahead of welcoming Sporting to the Emirates next week.

Should they continue their European journey, Arsenal will play the winner of Barcelona vs Atletico Madrid in the semi-finals on April 29.

But, despite not knowing which of the two Spanish sides they will face, flights to both Barcelona and Madrid have gone through the roof.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Fans were able to buy flights to Barcelona for as little as £15 before Tuesday’s victory, but prices are now hovering around the £200 mark.



While return flights to Madrid are nearing £250 after Atletico went 2-0 up over Barcelona in their quarter-final first leg last night.

Sports.title: England announce final two matches before World Cup 2026 with Florida friendlies vs New Zealand and 2014 tournament foes
Sports.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL is taking his England squad to the home of Mickey Mouse ahead of the World Cup.

The Three Lions will travel to Orlando to take on Costa Rica in a friendly at the Inter&Co Stadium on June 10.





This will be the squad’s final warm-up game before they travel to their Kansas base ahead of the June 17 opener against Croatia.

England will fly to Florida on June 1 for a training camp and the first friendly is against New Zealand at the Raymond James Stadium in Tampa on June 6.

Both games will kick off at 4pm local time which is 9pm British Summer Time.

England were due to play the second friendly at Inter Miami’s new stadium but after an agreement could not be reached and that included the MLS club’s recent temporary home in Fort Lauderdale – so it was agreed to switch the match to the home of MLS side Orlando City which has a 25,000 capacity.



England boss Tuchel has already revealed the Florida camp will be relaxed with the players allowed to mix with friends and family. Unusually, they might even be allowed to watch training.

Although once England arrive in Kansas, everything will become more focused ahead of the opening game against Croatia in Dallas.

Tuchel is set to name his squad after the end of the Premier League season on May 24, potentially May 26. All squads must be sent to FIFA by May 30, the day of the Champions League final.

England are in Group L with Croatia, Panama and Ghana, with the Three Lions overwhelming favourites to win the group.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Thomas Tuchel is aware that the Three Lions have not won the World Cup since 1966, and there is pressure to try to bring football home this summer.

In the last two editions, the Three Lions have shown impressive strength and consistency.

They finished fourth in 2018 under Gareth Southgate, before reaching the quarter-finals at Qatar 2022.

But there is a feeling that under Tuchel, who is seen as having more tactical nous, this team could finally take the final step and win the World Cup.

Sports.title: Suspended Chelsea star Enzo Fernandez issues grovelling apology to teammates over Real Madrid transfer bombshell
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ’S agent, Javier Pastore, has insisted there is ‘nothing’ in reports that he wants to join Real Madrid this summer.

That is despite numerous interviews over the international break, where Fernandez flirted with a move to Madrid and spoke about his love for the city.





Due to his actions, Fernandez, 25, was punished by Chelsea chiefs, including manager Liam Rosenior.

The attacking midfielder was sitting with the substitutes against Port Vale after being suspended by the club for two games, the second of which will be served against Manchester City this Sunday.

His agent felt as though the actions taken against Fernandez were unfair, and earlier this week spoke out against the ban.

And today, speaking to TopMercato.com, he opened up on Fernandez’s errors.

Former PSG star Pastore, 36, said: “We’ve already talked about this in recent days. These are statements he made without any intention of causing problems at Chelsea.

“He’s the vice-captain, one of the team’s leaders, and he’s shown his best form on the pitch this season.

“He was simply talking about a city. Then there were a lot of interviews in a short period where he talked about his future.

“The media mixed things up and started saying he was going to leave Chelsea. There’s absolutely nothing to it,”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“We’re on the same page with Chelsea. We made peace yesterday and the day before that, between Chelsea and the player.

“There were never really any problems. We cleared the air.”

The former PSG midfielder also delved into how Fernandez apologised in private to the club and his teammates.

And while it feels unlikely that Chelsea would reverse their decision and allow Fernandez to play any part against Manchester City, it’s good news for Blues supporters in any sense that the air has been cleared.

Pastore added: “What happened, happened.

“We explained to the player that, even though he hadn’t done anything wrong, he shouldn’t have said that. He’s only 25. He’s still young; he still has things to learn.

“We explained to the club that he said it without malice, that he made a mistake.

“He naturally apologised to the club, his teammates, the coach, the sporting director, and everyone.

“We’re all on the same page. We simply had to clear up the misunderstanding.”

Sports.title: Furious football chief tells fan of Man Utd offshoot to ‘go f**k yourself’ in X-rated email rant over ‘diabolical’ move
Sports.content:
A FOOTBALL league chairman told a supporter to “go f*** yourself” during an argument over a key fixture venue.

Aled Duckfield, a fan of FC United in Manchester, shared a screenshot of an email he received from Northern Premier League chairman Mark Harris that included the offensive language.





Duckfield had contacted Harris to complain after the NPL ruled that FC United’s important clash with Stockton Town would be moved to a neutral venue.

FC United trail the leaders by two points with a game in hand and four to go, while Stockton are one point outside the play-offs.

The game is now set for April 21.

But it’s been rescheduled six times due to issues with the playing surface at the purpose built, 4,900-capacity Broadhurst Park in Moston.



One of the postponed games came at the last hour – only ONE hour before kick-off – after Stockton had already made the 115-mile trip.

Though the fan-founded club, born from the 2005 Glazer takeover backlash, eventually covered their travel costs.

Officials from the rebel outfit put forward alternatives.

BUT they’ve now decided that the game will be played at the nearby home of Curzon Ashton.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Originally, it was thought that Curzon’s pitch would be the backup should something go wrong on the day.

Duckfield then got in contact with the NPL boss to call the decision “diabolical”, adding that the league “should be ashamed of yourselves”.

He wrote: “There is also the chance we could win the league at this fixture as well, and to take this away from our supporters from being in our own ground shows the incompetence and lack of governance present at the NPL.

“You clearly have an issue with us, maybe it’s because we know how to do things properly.”

The fan of the Man Utd offshoot even called for Harris to stand down.



Duckfield wrote: “You best believe you created a fire for us FC United supporters that, as you are aware, will not be put out.”

And it took only SIX minutes for Harris to reply.

In Duckfield’s X post, he revealed he received a reply from Harris at 21:27, sent from his official league email account.

The screenshot said: “Thank you for your lovely email. Now go f*** yourself.”

But Duckfield will not have been the only fan surprised by this reaction, as the club has averaged more than 1,800 fans this season.



Duckfield added: “I’m shocked by this response to my email from the Chair of the Northern Premier League and member of the FA Council.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Is this an acceptable way for those in power to speak to football supporters who express genuine concerns?”

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Wayne Rooney reveals his incredible top six sports stars of all time… including one who SACKED him
Sports.content:
WAYNE ROONEY has revealed his top six greatest sports stars of all time, and included a figure who once played a role in ending his managerial spell.

The Manchester United legend made the admission while speaking on The Wayne Rooney Show.





And in a surprising twist, Rooney deliberately left footballers out of his list entirely, despite being one of the Premier League’s all-time greats.

Instead, he turned his attention to icons from across the wider sporting world.

At number one, Rooney picked snooker genius Ronnie O’Sullivan, admitting his choice might divide opinion.

He said: “My number one is, it’s controversial but, for me, I absolutely love him, it’s Ronnie O’Sullivan. I love snooker, I’ve always loved snooker.

“In snooker, you’ve had some absolute legends. Jimmy White, Stephen Hendry, absolute legends in snooker.”

Rooney then placed golf icon Tiger Woods second on his list.

Former heavyweight world champion Mike Tyson came in at number three.



Tennis legend Serena Williams was ranked fourth by the ex-England captain.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But it was his fifth choice that raised eyebrows.

Rooney included NFL superstar Tom Brady, who is part of the ownership group at Birmingham City and was at the club when Rooney was sacked as manager.

Basketball great Michael Jordan completed Rooney’s top six.

Despite his own legendary football career, Rooney’s list made it clear he was keen to shine a light on sporting icons from beyond the pitch, even if one of them had a hand in his own downfall.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich to rival Arsenal and Man Utd in Morgan Rogers transfer battle
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich to rival Arsenal and Man Utd in Morgan Rogers transfer battle

Morgan Rogers has enjoyed another fine season for Aston Villa and the England star is attracting transfer interest from some of the Premier League and Europe's biggest clubs

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers is attracting interest from some of Europe's biggest clubs (Image: Marc Atkins/Aston Villa FC)

Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United are all ready to test Aston Villa's resolve over Morgan Rogers in the summer transfer window but will face competition from Bayern Munich for the attacking midfielder.

Rogers, 23, has been a revelation since moving to Villa Park from Championship Middlesbrough in February 2024, recording 24 goals and 23 assists since the start of last season. His excellent form prompted Villa to tie him down to a new contract back in November - but that has not deterred interest from some of their Premier League's rivals and Europe's elite.

Both Arsenal and United are keen on adding a quality left-sided forward option to their respective squads in the summer transfer window, with Rogers comfortable in several attacking positions. Chelsea, like Arsenal, made their interest known in Rogers last summer and also retain a strong interest in the England star.

Mirror Football understands that Bayern Munich are also admirers of Rogers, who impressed in the Champions League for Villa last year. And they could offer him the chance to continue his upward trajectory overseas as part of the swashbuckling team that has plundered 100 Bundesliga goals already this term under Vincent Kompany.

Arsenal star makes unexpected return to training in big title race boost READ MORE :

Man Utd face handing over millions to Man City after Elliot Anderson decision READ MORE :

While Rogers' profile and value could rise significantly with a strong showing at the World Cup, Villa would demand in excess of £80million to part ways with the 2024-25 PFA Young Player of the Season.

And while Villa would be reluctant to lose a player of Rogers' quality, selling him for such a mammoth sum would help soothe financial concerns.

It has been documented in recent weeks that Manchester United are working on targets for the left wing position as well as an overhaul of their central midfield options in a summer where they will also appoint a permanent manager.

View 2 Images Rogers has enjoyed a fine season for club and country and may attract interest ahead of the World Cup (Image: Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

Arsenal are also expected to refresh their attack in the summer and are long-term admirers of Rogers, who was linked with a stunning transfer last summer.

The Gunners would likely decide to cash in on either Leandro Trossard or Gabriel Martinelli, their current left wing options, in order to finance a move for Rogers and space for him within their squad.

The former has just a year remaining on his current contract at The Emirates, while Martinelli has struggled to rediscover the type of form that made him a key figure in Mikel Arteta's team previously, scoring just once in the Premier League this season.

Sports.title: Southampton allowed to break FA Cup rules for semi-final against Man City
Sports.content:
Southampton allowed to break FA Cup rules for semi-final against Man City

Southampton will face Manchester City in the semi-finals of the FA Cup later this month, but the Saints won't be wearing their traditional red and white stripes

View 2 Images Southampton have won yellow in the FA Cup this season (Image: Matt Watson/Southampton FC via Getty Images)

Southampton have been granted permission to wear their special anniversary kit for their FA Cup semi-final against Manchester City. The Saints have worn the yellow strip throughout this season's competition, including at home, such as when they beat Arsenal 2-1 in the quarter-finals last weekend.

‌



Inspired by their 4-0 victory over Manchester United in the 1976 FA Cup final, the shirt is predominantly yellow with blue trim and marks Southampton's only major trophy win. But its use at Wembley was in doubt, as FA rules state that from the semi-final stage onwards, clubs must wear a kit which was registered at the start of the season.

‌



Now, though, Southampton have announced that they'll be able to wear yellow when they face City on Saturday, April 25. Southampton said: "The club is pleased to have been granted permission to wear the commemorative '76-inspired yellow kit that has been a permanent fixture of this season's FA Cup run for the victories over Doncaster, Leicester, Fulham and Arsenal."

‌



In another good omen for the Saints, they've been granted the west end of Wembley. That's where their fans watched them beat Leeds in the 2024 Championship play-off final.

FA Cup semi-final fixture details confirmed after Chelsea vs Leeds concerns READ MORE :

Premier League fixture changes confirmed with FA Cup semi-final impact clear READ MORE :

Tonda Eckert's men pulled off a famous win against Arsenal on Saturday to book their ticket to Wembley. Goals from Ross Stewart and Shea Charles either side of Viktor Gyokeres' equaliser got the job done at a raucous St Mary's.

‌



The winner of their semi-final will play either Chelsea or Leeds in this year's final on Saturday, May 16. Southampton are also chasing promotion to the Premier League, having suffered relegation back to the Championship last term.

The Saints beat promotion rivals Wrexham 5-1 on Tuesday to leapfrog their opponents and move into the play-off spots. Southampton also have a game in hand on all but one of the teams in the play-off mix.

Who'll reach the FA Cup final? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

"I think we are at a good moment physically and mentally, but we will need to close this game tonight, recover tomorrow and go again," Eckert, who was appointed in December after a successful interim spell, hailed.

"I think when you come to this stage of the season you need everyone being ready to go. The group lives off a very good spirit, you can feel that. We travelled yesterday, and with the focus that we had in the morning session today, you could see that the boys were ready. That’s good to know for the games going forward."

Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard injury latest as Arsenal boost emerges despite training absence

Martin Odegaard suffered a knee problem against Sporting CP and missed Arsenal training on Thursday, but Norway boss Stale Solbakken does not believe the injury is serious. Arsenal received a major boost with Eberechi Eze returning to training ahead of the Bournemouth clash.

View 2 Images Martin Odegaard appeared to suffer a knock during Arsenal's clash against Sporting CP (Image: Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

Norway manager Stale Solbakken has played down concerns over Martin Odegaard's latest injury setback. Arsenal suffered another blow when their captain was substituted during the match against Sporting CP.

‌



Odegaard required medical attention after experiencing knee discomfort and was subsequently withdrawn in favour of Kai Havertz. He seemed to walk off the pitch without difficulty, though the Gunners' talisman was absent from Thursday's training session.

‌



The 27-year-old had only just returned at the weekend following more than a month on the sidelines. He featured in the FA Cup loss to Southampton before being named in the starting XI against Sporting.

‌



Odegaard was unavailable for Norway's fixtures against the Netherlands and Switzerland in the build-up to this summer's World Cup. The ex-Real Sociedad startlet had been sidelined since Arsenal's north London derby encounter with Tottenham in February.

Solbakken has sought to ease worries surrounding any problem Odegaard may have picked up. Speaking at a press conference at Ullevaal Stadium, he doesn't believe it's a serious concern.

Arsenal star makes unexpected return to training in big title race boost READ MORE :

"He got a little one (bang) where he shouldn't have gotten it, but I don't think it's pitch black," he said. "We don't need any more setbacks now," he added.

Former Norway defender Jesper Mathisen had previously expressed alarm on TV2. "Those are scary images," he said after Odegaard went down.

"Like watching a horror movie. A nightmare. He's not sitting down for no reason. It would have been a big loss for both Arsenal and Norway if he had to go out with an injury again."

Premier League star admits footballers DM him over team news for Fantasy Football

Fantasy Football has become a hugely popular game which has grown over several years alongside the popularity of the Premier League

Fulham star Harry Wilson has revealed that Wales teammates message him over team news for their Fantasy Football squads. The forward has enjoyed an impressive season for Marco Silva's team as they seek European qualification.

The Cottagers currently sit seventh in the Premier League table - three points off seventh-placed Brentford, which will guarantee a spot in next season's Europa Conference League. Wilson has been a key player for Silva's team, with 10 league goals and six assists, aiding Fulham's charge for Europe.

The 29-year-old's performances for his club have drawn the attention of those playing popular online game Fantasy Football. The game see players picking their team of Premier League stars for the next game week, with points accrued by the individual performances of those they have chosen.

FA Cup semi-final fixture details confirmed after Chelsea vs Leeds concerns READ MORE :

And the Welsh international has opened up to BBC Sport over how his impressive form across the season has led to messages on social media from those asking to see if he will be picked for a certain match.

He said: "My Instagram DMs have been full. I had a little injury a couple of weeks ago and the amount of messages from people saying, 'are you playing on the weekend'.

Sports.title: Diego Simeone proves again why he's the man all elite Premier League sides should want
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone proves again why he's the man all elite Premier League sides should want

The Argentine coach has been at Atletico Madrid for more than 14 years and might be ready for a new challenge - even though his love affair with the Spanish club continues

View 3 Images Diego Simeone led Atletico Madrid to a win at Barcelona in the first leg of their Champions League quarter-final (Image: Getty Images)

In light of the Champions League results on Wednesday night, it would be easy to put two-nil and two-nil together and come up with Diego Simeone for Liverpool. It is not the most fanciful shout.

‌



Bookmakers being bookmakers - anything to make an extra pound - they are offering odds on who will succeed Arne Slot, even though the guy is still in the job. And for what it is worth, I think the Premier League triumph of 2024/25 should give Slot enough credit to start next season at Anfield, regardless of what happens in the remaining seven weeks of the current campaign.

‌



But even his most ardent supporters would have to admit the signs do not look good for Slot. Which is why there is trade in the next-Liverpool-manager market.

‌



Florian Wirtz gets blunt message from Jamie Carragher as Thierry Henry can't contain laughter READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso is the odds-on favourite and Simeone is among the outsiders, currently priced at 20-1. But the idea is not too outrageous.

Simeone has been Atletico Madrid’s manager since December 2011, and it really is hard to imagine him anywhere else. But his current contract only runs until the summer of 2027.

While the Champions League win at the Nou Camp on Wednesday was a fantastic result, last Sunday’s home defeat to Barcelona left them 19 points adrift of Hansi Flick's La Liga leaders. He turns 56 later this month and could be ready for a new challenge.

‌



The managerial market could again be interesting this summer. The suggestions that Pep Guardiola will call time on his Manchester City era at the end of this season remain strong, and in theory, the Manchester United job will be available, even though you would have to say Michael Carrick looks well-positioned for that one.

View 3 Images Arne Slot is facing increasing pressure after the defeat in Paris (Image: (Photo by Dave Winter/Shutterstock))

Slot is obviously under severe pressure and don’t think Liam Rosenoir’s long-term deal will stop him being in the firing line of Chelsea do not have a good end to the season. Again, the most realistic long-term scenario for Simeone is an extension of his time in Madrid.

‌



Alternatively, he has expressed an interest in going back to Serie A, where he enjoyed a lot of his playing time. And his very limited grasp of English has always been seen as a barrier to a move to the Premier League.

But he would still be a compelling addition to a competition which needs any compelling addition it can get. Over almost a decade and a half at Atletico, he has taken charge of 788 games, recording 466 wins, 170 draws and 152 losses.

From 2013-14 onwards, after winning the first of their two La Liga titles under Simeone, Atletico have qualified for the Champions League every season, twice falling to agonising final defeats at the hands of Real Madrid in the space of three years between 2014 and 2016. But if any interested Premier League club wanted further proof of his managerial qualities, they should catch up with the press conference he gave ahead of the 2-0 win in Barcelona in the Champions League.

‌



View 3 Images Xabi Alonso is the odds-on favourite to be the next Liverpool manager if Arne Slot leaves Anfield (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

Sat next to the Frenchman, Simeone paid tribute to Antoine Griezmann, who is leaving Atletico for MLS side Orlando City SC at the end of the season. The subtitles move you to tears, I swear.

“I want to thank you for your hard work and humility,” he told Griezmann. "You are an admirable person in a society where young people need role models like you.

Article continues below

“Thank you for your commitment, for knowing how to distinguish between the friendship we share and the professional relationship between a coach and a player. I view you first as a player and only then as a friend. I love you but you know that if you don’t run tomorrow, you are out.”

It was a perfectly-pitched tribute and gave an insight into why players run through brick walls for Simeone. If any elite Premier League club is looking for a new manager this summer, they should be beating a path to Diego’s door.

Sports.title: Liverpool fans issue statement ahead of Anfield protest: 'Do the right thing'
Sports.content:
Liverpool fans issue statement ahead of Anfield protest: 'Do the right thing'

Liverpool fans will protest against the club's plan to increase ticket prices when they welcome Fulham to Anfield on Saturday, and the Kop End will look very different

View Image Liverpool supporters will protest on Saturday (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

Liverpool fan group Spion Kop 1906 have announced that they will remove their flags and banners from the Kop End on Saturday as part of a planned protest against rising ticket prices. Last month, the club announced that the cost of tickets will increase in line with inflation over the next three years.

‌



The decision sparked backlash from fans and Liverpool supporters' union, Spirit of Shankly, subsequently announced a protest for their home game against Fulham. The group launched a campaign called 'not a pound in the ground', urging fans not to spend any money inside Anfield.

‌



Now, Spion Kop 1906 have announced their own form of protest. In a statement released on Thursday, they said: "Since the announcement regarding future ticket pricing, we have been in discussions as a group regarding our response.

‌



"As always, we will pay our respects at the closest game to the anniversary of the Hillsborough disaster, which will be the PSG game (on Tuesday, April 14). After much consultation, all Spion Kop 1906 flags will no longer be present at Anfield at the remaining fixtures.

"We must take a stand against the rising cost of football, we feel there's a value to being valued. The culture and traditions, which have been passed down by previous generations must be preserved, with football remaining accessible to future generations.

"We, the fans, are the heartbeat of the football club; the same heartbeat that Liverpool Football Club market for a pound note. We urge FSG to remember that our club should embody the identity of its surrounding community and resonate with the values of the local area.
